verdict.rationale: Evidence confirms the core engine is MIT-licensed and open source (playcanvas-probe-rt-2's 'MIT engine runtime' and community confirmation in playcanvas-comm-11), meaning no royalties or per-install fees on shipped games. However, the hosted Editor/cloud platform runs on a paid subscription tier system (private projects require payment, and features like REST API access, project archive/restore are plan-gated), which is a real caveat for studios relying on the cloud tooling even though it's unrelated to game revenue. Missing for 10: an explicit license text/SPDX citation for the engine repo, and clearer separation in docs distinguishing engine licensing from platform subscription costs.
